source: The Bogleheads Variable Percentage Withdrawal (VPW) table: the share of a portfolio to withdraw each year so that a real-return assumption depletes it by 100, rising with age; figures here are in the region of the published 60/40 and 40/60 columns.
confidenceNote: Recalled from the shape of the published table and rounded to a tenth of a point; interpolated between the ages listed. VPW is a method, not a guarantee: a bad decade shrinks every later withdrawal. The spend-curve decline after 70 is a separate planning convention, not part of VPW.
note: percentages: annual withdrawal as a decimal fraction of the portfolio at the start of the year, by age, for two stock shares; the engine interpolates by age and picks the nearer column by stock share. spendDeclineAfterAge / spendDeclinePerYear: real spending falls this fraction a year past that age. planAge: the age the plan is run to. D-087.
